sentences.text: The Petitioners have filed these Two petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road accident dated 06.07.2020.
Both petitions have arisen out of a common accident.

Therefore, both the petitions have been clubbed together as per order dated 21.04.2022 for common trial and common judgment is passed.
SCCH-25 2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is as follows: On 06/07.02.2020 at about 12.30am the petitioners in both the cases were proceeding in a motorcycle bearing No.KA54E5908 as a rider and pillion rider near Alankar Daba, Malaluru ring Road, Kempegowda Nagar, Tumakuru.

At that time a Lorry bearing Reg.NO.KA17C7846 driven by its driver with a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life suddenly applied brake and stopped the Lorry without showing any traffic indications leading to Tremendous impact to the said motorcycle, which was behind the Lorry and caused the accident.
Due to impact both the petitioners fell down and suffered grievous injuries and they were taken to the hospital and treated.
The Jurisdictional Tumkuru Traffic Police have registered a case and filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending Lorry.
Therefore, the Respondents being the insurer and the RC owner of the offending Lorry are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
SCCH-25 3.
In response to notices issued by this tribunal, the Respondent No.2 appeared and filed Objections.
In spite of due service of summons, the Respondent No.1 did not appear hence, placed exparte.

4. The objections of the Respondent No.1:
It has denied the case of the petitioner as false but admitted issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.

It has further submitted that there is noncompliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act.

It has further submitted that the driver of the Lorry did not have valid and effective DL, permit and FC as on the date of accident and also denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the Lorry.
It has contended that the accident was caused due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.

sentences.text: During the cross examination of Pw.1 he has admitted that it is a double road but also narrow road.
He has further admitted that as per the records he was moving on the middle of the road.
He has stated that the brake lights of the Lorry did not blink.
During the cross examination of Pw.2 nothing worthwhile showing the absence of negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry is elicited.
10. The date of accident is 06/07.02.2020 at 12.30am and the FIR was registered on 07.02.2020 at 03.00pm against the rider of the Two wheeler and the driver of the Lorry.
The spot SCCH-25 mahazar was conducted on the same day from 4.00 to 5.20pm.

As per Ex.P.5 IMV report, the Lorry was damaged to its rear right side, brake light, grill bent inwards and damaged along with registration number plate and the bike was damaged to front left side, head light mask, left side fuel tank, left side crashguard, bent inwards and damaged, left side clutch bent and damaged.

As per Exs.P.3 & 14 the petitioners in both the cases have suffered injuries in RTA.
11.
The respondent has admitted that the accident has taken place and that the petitioners have suffered injuries.
The only dispute by the respondent is about the aspect of negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
In order to prove the same, the respondents neither examined any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decision : 2014 AIR SCW 1709 : Smt. Meera Devi & Anr. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation Ltd., "Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has held on facts of the case that there was no contributory negligence of the deceased".

sentences.text: However, on the basis of the documents before the court, I hold that the petitioners in both the cases suffered injuries as per their wound certificates and the accident was caused due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry.
Accordingly, issue No.1 in both the cases are held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2 In MVC 4135/2020:
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, he has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.14.

He has also got examined Dr.Keerthi Shivalingaiah as PW.4, who has given the details of the injury and the surgery undergone by the petitioner and he has stated that the whole body physical disability is 10% and the permanent physical impairment of lower limb is 30.2%.
During his cross examination he has admitted that the petitioner is not under any medication.
He has also admitted that the loss of mobility and stability are very mild.
Petitioner has stated that he is a student, studying I year B.Com at SSIT.
The disability being SCCH-25 suffered by him will affect his day today activities and also his Academics.
But the petitioner has open grade Both Bone communited fracture right proximal Tibia which will affect his movement of right leg.

Therefore, the Tribunal deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 5% Monthly income:

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Bharathi Hospital,
wherein he was treated as an inpatient from SCCH-25 07.02.2020 to 12.02.2020.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries he has undergone simple and grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/ under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,

In this regard,
he has produced Seventeen medical bills as per Ex.P.15 for a sum of Rs.1,11,729/.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents to disprove the medical expenses by the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 6 days at Bharathi Hospital, Tumkur.
In this regard he has not produced discharge summary, but it can be seen by wound SCCH-25 certificate of Bharathi Hospital at Ex.P.14 that he has taken treatment in that hospital.

Therefore,
considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
As on the date of accident he was 20 years old.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable for his age is 18.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,62,000/
(Rs.15,000/ x 12 x 18 x 5% = Rs.1,62,000/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 20 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained simple and grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 5% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability SCCH-25 throughout his life.
He will suffer in his mind that he is no more a normal man.
This will have an adverse effect on the future life of the petitioner.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.

SCCH-25 ORDER
The petitions in MVC No.4135/2020 and 4137/2020 are hereby allowed with cost.

However the Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount to the Petitioners within 60 days from today.
